The skin depth ($\delta$) is given by the formula: $\delta = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\omega \mu \sigma}}$ where angular frequency $\omega = 2\pi f$. Given: $f = 10^{10}\text{ Hz}$, $\sigma = 2 \times 10^7\text{ S/m}$, and $\mu \approx \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ H/m}$.

1. Calculate $\omega$: 
   $$\omega = 2 \pi \times 10^{10} = 2\pi \times 10^{10}\text{ rad/s}$$
2. Substitute values into the skin depth formula:
   $$\delta = \sqrt{\frac{2}{(2\pi \times 10^{10}) \times (4\pi \times 10^{-7}) \times (2 \times 10^7)}}$$
   $$\delta = \sqrt{\frac{2}{16\pi^2 \times 10^{10}}} = \frac{1}{4\pi \times 10^5} \approx 2.53 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m} \text{ or } 0.253\text{ \mu m}$$.
proTip: Always substitute standard units and double-check your $\pi^2$ simplification during numerical calculations.
